land.text: the Later Tang realm, which Shi Jingtang took after Li Congke's fall on 11 January 937 (Later Tang infobox)

predecessors.note: Shi Jingtang 'rose in rebellion against then-Later Tang emperor' Li Congke in 936 (Shi Chonggui page) and 'became emperor in this same year' with Liao aid (Five Dynasties page); Sichuan was already Later Shu.

land.text: the Later Han realm, Liu Zhiyuan's state proclaimed in 947

successors.note: The Later Jin page names Later Han and the Liao as successors but is silent on Liu Zhiyuan; the Five Dynasties page says 'Liu Zhiyuan proclaimed Later Han in 947' and that the Khitans withdrew early in 947.

land.text: Kaifeng and the Hebei plain, taken by the Khitan in January 947

successors.note: The Later Jin page: the Liao 'annihilated the Later Jin and annexed its former territories' and was officially renamed 'Great Liao'; the Khitan withdrew in 947.

capitals.name: Taiyuan
capitals.note: Infobox 'Taiyuan (936)'; Shi Jingtang held Hedong from Taiyuan from 932 (Shi Chonggui page).

capitals.name: Luoyang
capitals.note: Infobox 'Luoyang (937)'; 'Shi Jingtang then entered Luoyang unopposed' after Li Congke's suicide (Shi Chonggui page).

capitals.name: Kaifeng (Daliang)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kaifeng (937-947)'; 'Later in 937, Shi Jingtang summoned Shi Chonggui to then-capital Kaifeng' (Shi Chonggui page).

rulers.name: Gaozu (Shi Jingtang)
rulers.note: Infobox 936-942; proclaimed emperor by Liao 28 November 936.

rulers.name: Shi Chonggui (Emperor Chu)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: July 28, 942 - January 11, 947'; surrendered the seals to Liao on 11 January 947.

correction.text: the Hedong state of Jin under Li Keyong and Li Cunxu, 911-921, to be drawn under the slug former-jin

keyframe_review.note: Not Shi Jingtang's Later Jin: the Later Jin was founded in 936 ('Founded in 936 by Shi Jingtang'). Cliopatria's 71,612 km2 shape for 911-921 (Shanxi north of Taiyuan, 33 percent of Shanxi) is Li Keyong's and Li Cunxu's Jin: 'Li Keyong, jiedushi of the Hedong circuit (Shanxi), formed the polity of Jin'. It belongs to the Jin dossier (slug former-jin, Wikipedia 'Jin (Later Tang precursor)'), which has no row for these years of its own because Cliopatria filed them under 'Later Jin'.

correction.text: Shanxi (Hedong, Shi Jingtang's command from Taiyuan since 932) without the northern prefectures ceded to Liao

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 936 alone (28 November-31 December 936): the state is Shi Jingtang's Hedong command round his capital Taiyuan ('Taiyuan (936)'); Li Congke's Later Tang fell only on 11 January 937 (Later Tang infobox), so Luoyang and Kaifeng were not yet Later Jin's. Cliopatria draws the full 790,319 km2 realm from 936.

union.text: the Sixteen Prefectures (Beijing, Tianjin, northern Hebei and northern Shanxi): the land Cliopatria adds to the Liao shape in 936 inside those four units

correction.text: the Later Jin realm of 937: the Later Tang heartland without Sichuan, still with the Sixteen Prefectures

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 937: the realm is the Cliopatria 936 shape plus the Sixteen Prefectures, which the Sixteen Prefectures page says passed to the Liao in 938 ('In 938 AD, the prefectures were ceded to the Khitans by Shi Jingtang'; once '937'). The Five Dynasties page says he 'promised' them in 936 and the Later Jin page gives no date, so the cession year is disputed (936, 937, 938).

Valid for 938-947, shape unchanged, years extended to 947: the page says the Later Jin 'held essentially the same territories as Later Tang, except Sichuan', less the Sixteen Prefectures; the state ended on 11 January 947 ('Emperor Chu's surrender to Liao: 11 January, 947'), a year after Cliopatria's last year, 946. The infobox gives no area, so no ratio; Cliopatria's 790,319 km2 equals its Later Han 947 shape.

region.text: Shanxi (Hedong, Shi Jingtang's command from Taiyuan since 932) without the northern prefectures ceded to Liao

ledger.note: 936: Shi Jingtang is proclaimed emperor of the Later Jin, with Khitan help. Infobox 'Shi Jingtang proclaimed Emperor by Liao: 28 November, 936', capital Taiyuan (936). The page names the capital, not a boundary; Hedong (Shanxi) is his command from Taiyuan since 932 (Shi Chonggui page).

region.text: the Later Jin realm as it stood under Liao suzerainty: the Cliopatria 936 shape (from January 937 the Later Tang heartland without Sichuan; the Sixteen Prefectures until 938)

ledger.note: 28 November 936: the Later Jin is founded as a Liao client. The page: the state was 'founded by Shi Jingtang ... with aid from the Liao dynasty, which assumed suzerainty over the Later Jin' and 'had often been described as a puppet of the emerging Khitan-led Liao dynasty' (infobox: 'Shi Jingtang proclaimed Emperor by Liao: 28 November, 936'). The Taizong page, second page: Shi 'referred to himself as "subject" and "son," while referring to Emperor Taizong as "father emperor"' and agreed to an annual silk tribute. The page gives no year for the suzerainty as such; the date is the proclamation. Vassal tint, not territory of the Liao.

union.text: the Sixteen Prefectures (Beijing, Tianjin, northern Hebei and northern Shanxi): the land Cliopatria adds to the Liao shape in 936 inside those four units

minus.text: the Later Jin realm of 937: the Later Tang heartland without Sichuan, still with the Sixteen Prefectures
Shanxi (Hedong, Shi Jingtang's command from Taiyuan since 932) without the northern prefectures ceded to Liao

region.text: the Later Tang realm outside Hedong and Sichuan, with the Sixteen Prefectures

ledger.note: 937: the Later Tang heartland comes over after Li Congke's fall. 'The Later Jin held essentially the same territories as Later Tang, except Sichuan, which had become independent as Later Shu.' The month (January) is the Later Tang infobox's ('January 11, 937'), not this page's, so none is stored; the Shi Chonggui page: Shi 'entered Luoyang unopposed' after Li Congke's suicide.
937: the capital moves from Taiyuan to Luoyang. Infobox 'Taiyuan (936) Luoyang (937) Kaifeng (937-947)'.
937: the capital moves on to Kaifeng. Infobox 'Kaifeng (937-947)'; 'Later in 937, Shi Jingtang summoned Shi Chonggui to then-capital Kaifeng' (Shi Chonggui page).

region.text: the Tianxiong circuit, headquartered at Yedu

ledger.note: 937: Fan Yanguang rebels in Tianxiong. 'He launched his troops in summer 937 and headed toward the Yellow River ford at Liyang'; Zhang Congbin joined him and took 'both Heyang Circuit and Luoyang itself'; Yang Guangyuan crushed Fan's army at the crossing and Fan withdrew to Yedu. The page puts the revolt in 937 and gives no month for its outbreak; the Yedu country is drawn as an 80 km disc.

region.text: the Sixteen Prefectures (Beijing, Tianjin, northern Hebei and northern Shanxi): the land Cliopatria adds to the Liao shape in 936 inside those four units

ledger.note: 938: the Sixteen Prefectures pass to the Khitan. 'In 938 AD, the prefectures were ceded to the Khitans by Shi Jingtang' (once '937'); 'The Sixteen Prefectures passed into Liao hands in 938'. The Five Dynasties page has him 'promised' the cession, with tribute, in return for Liao aid in 936; the Later Jin page says the Khitan 'forced the Later Jin to cede the strategic Sixteen Prefectures' with no date. Cliopatria's Liao shape holds the land from 936. The Taizong page, a second page, puts the agreement in the 936 account ('As part of Shi's enthronement announcement, he announced the agreement to cede Lulong and parts of Hedong ... for a total of 16 prefectures') without a year for the handover, which agrees with 'promised 936, ceded 938'.

region.text: the Tianxiong circuit, headquartered at Yedu

ledger.note: Fall 938: Fan Yanguang surrenders Yedu. 'A subsequent siege of Yedu by Later Jin forces dragged on to fall 938'; Fan 'opened the city and surrendered', was made military governor of Tianping and Prince of Dongping, went to Daliang in winter 938 and was drowned in the Yellow River in 940. The page gives no month.

region.text: the Later Jin realm as it stood under Liao suzerainty: the Cliopatria 936 shape (from January 937 the Later Tang heartland without Sichuan; the Sixteen Prefectures until 938)

ledger.note: Summer 942: Shi Chonggui breaks the subordination. After Shi Jingtang's death in summer 942 (Taizong page) and Shi Chonggui's accession, he wrote to Taizong 'indicating equal status and not subservience', calling himself 'grandson' 'but not as "your subject"'; Taizong was angered and sent emissaries to rebuke him. The Five Dynasties page dates the Khitan declaration of war to 943 and the Taizong page has Yang Guangyuan urging an attack 'by winter 943'; the first invasion is early 944 (the contest_start of 944). The page gives no month for the letter.

region.text: the Hebei plain up to the Yedu region

ledger.note: 944: the Liao invade the Hebei plain. 'In early 944, Emperor Taizong led a major invasion into Later Jin territory, and quickly reached Yedu'; a second invasion in late 944 advanced 'all the way to the Yedu region, but soon withdrew again'. The Five Dynasties page has the Khitan declare war in 943. The page gives no month; Yedu is read as the Daming country in southern Hebei.

region.text: the Hebei plain up to Kaifeng

ledger.note: 947: Kaifeng falls to the Liao. 'Shi Chonggui surrendered the imperial seals that day to Emperor Taizong of Liao' (footnote: 11 January 947); 'Emperor Taizong subsequently entered Daliang'. Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen had surrendered their army at Zhongdu Bridge in 946.

region.text: the Later Jin realm, annexed by the Liao in January 947

ledger.note: 947: the Liao take the Later Jin realm. The page: the Liao 'annihilated the Later Jin and annexed its former territories in 947'; it is silent on the Khitan withdrawal and on Liu Zhiyuan, whom the Five Dynasties page dates to the same year ('they withdrew early the next year (947)'; 'Liu Zhiyuan proclaimed Later Han in 947').

region.text: the Later Jin realm at its end

ledger.note: 947: the Later Jin ends. Infobox 'Emperor Chu's surrender to Liao: 11 January, 947'; successors the Later Han and the Liao.

wars.name: Shi Jingtang's revolt against Later Tang

zones.text: the Sixteen Prefectures (Beijing, Tianjin, northern Hebei and northern Shanxi): the land Cliopatria adds to the Liao shape in 936 inside those four units

wars.outcome: Shi Jingtang overthrew Li Congke (Later Tang ended 11 January 937) with Khitan aid and gave the Liao the Sixteen Prefectures and annual tribute.
wars.note: 'Shi Jingtang rebelled against Li Congke with Khitan Liao aid and became emperor in this same year'; the Later Tang page dates the fall to 11 January 937.

wars.name: Liao-Later Jin war

zones.text: the Hebei plain: Yedu (early and late 944), Yangcheng (late 944), Zhongdu Bridge (946)

wars.outcome: Liao victory: the army at Zhongdu Bridge surrendered in 946 and Kaifeng fell on 11 January 947; Shi Chonggui was exiled to Huanglong; the Liao withdrew within the year.
wars.note: The Five Dynasties page: 'In 943 the Khitans declared war.' The Shi Chonggui page dates the invasions to early 944, late 944 and 946; it names no battle in 945 beyond Du Chongwei leaving Shunguo.

wars.name: An Congjin's rebellion
wars.outcome: Crushed: An Congjin rebelled after Shi Jingtang left Kaifeng and later committed suicide; no border moved.
wars.note: The page ties the rebellion to late 941 ('When An Congjin did rebel after Shi Jingtang left Kaifeng').

wars.name: Fan Yanguang's revolt

zones.text: the Tianxiong circuit, headquartered at Yedu

wars.outcome: Crushed by siege: Fan's army was beaten at the Yellow River crossing in 937, Yedu was besieged to fall 938 and Fan surrendered; Zhang Congbin, who joined him and took Heyang and Luoyang, was beaten too.
wars.note: The page names no battle at Yedu itself and no besieging commander; Fan held Tianxiong from the revolt in 937 to his surrender in fall 938, about a year, which makes a rebel dossier (type rebel) the other batch's job.

certainty.note: No treaty line on any opened page. The Liao suzerainty (28 November 936 to summer 942: a 'puppet' state, its emperor 'subject' and 'son' to a 'father emperor') is a diplomatic relation with no boundary of its own and is drawn as the lighter vassal tint over the whole realm. The northern frontier along the ceded Sixteen Prefectures (938) is the one named line, but its course comes from Cliopatria's Liao shape.
The suzerainty has ended and the war of 944-947 moves the front over the Hebei plain; no line is on any page. The northern frontier is as before.

sources.note: Opened for the thin finding on the Yedu revolt: summer 937 march, Zhang Congbin's seizure of Heyang and Luoyang, the siege of Yedu to fall 938, surrender and winter 938 journey to Daliang. No month anywhere.

sources.title: Emperor Taizong of Liao
sources.note: Opened for the thin finding on the Sixteen Prefectures and for the suzerainty: the 936 enthronement agreement ('a total of 16 prefectures' and annual silk tribute), Shi Jingtang as 'subject' and 'son', the break after Shi Chonggui's accession, Yang Guangyuan's urging by winter 943, the spring 944 incursion. No year for the handover of the prefectures.

notes: Cliopatria's Later Jin row has two unrelated shapes: 911-921 (71,612 km2, Shanxi) is the Jin of Li Keyong and Li Cunxu, the Later Tang's precursor, and is marked wrong here; 936-946 is Shi Jingtang's state. The Jin precursor needs 911-921 (and 922-925 as Cliopatria's Former Jin row) in the former-jin dossier, which is written by another batch; this dossier does not claim the 911 shape. Wikidata Q1154540 and Q6201794 (Former Jin) are as Cliopatria gives them. Dates: the Later Tang page puts the Later Tang's fall at 11 January 937, the Five Dynasties page says 936 for Shi Jingtang's rise; this dossier starts the state on 28 November 936 (the Later Jin page) and gives the Later Tang heartland to it on 11 January 937, which makes 936 a Hedong-only year (new keyframe 936b). The Sixteen Prefectures: the pages say 936 (promised), 937 or 938 (ceded) and the Later Jin page gives no date; the ledger follows the dedicated page (938) with confidence 2, and the 937 keyframe still holds the land. The Liao dossier (ea-05) should agree: Cliopatria's Liao shape holds the land from 936, so either its gain is 936-938 or the 936 and 937 Liao keyframes are adjusted. The Sixteen Prefectures region is Cliopatria's own addition to the Liao shape in 936 inside Hebei, Shanxi, Beijing and Tianjin (about 204,000 km2); the real prefectures cover less. The infobox gives no area; Cliopatria's 790,319 km2 equals the Later Han 947 shape. The Later Jin's vassalage to the Liao is in the ledger from the fix round (vassal_start 936/11, vassal_end 942): the Liao dossier should carry the mirror pair with the Later Jin as the vassal. Left out for lack of a dated page: the Southern Tang, Wuyue and Chu tributaries (the Shi Chonggui infobox lists Southern Tang and Wuyue as co-sovereigns in Fujian 945-947, de jure), the end of Shi Jingtang's line. The page is silent on Liu Zhiyuan's Later Han and on the Khitan withdrawal. FIX ROUND (2026-10-19): (1) vassal_start at 28 November 936 (Later Jin page: the Liao 'assumed suzerainty over the Later Jin'; 'puppet') and vassal_end in 942 (Shi Chonggui page: after his accession in summer 942 he wrote as 'grandson' 'but not as your subject'), both with counterpart liao-dynasty at confidence 2; the earlier note gave 943 as the end of the tribute, the first notes took it from the Five Dynasties page's declaration of war in 943, which is a year after the break of tone. The certainty list is split at 942 to carry the vassal period. (2) Thin item, Fan Yanguang (opened): the revolt was in 937 (summer march to the Liyang ford; Zhang Congbin took Heyang Circuit and Luoyang), Fan fell back to Yedu and surrendered after a siege 'to fall 938'; no month on the page. It is a contest_start 937 and contest_end 938 against 'Fan Yanguang's revolt (Tianxiong)' (a free string: no dossier). Fan held the Tianxiong circuit for about a year, so a rebel dossier is the other batch's job (counterparts_needing_dossiers); if one is written, the contest counterpart should become its slug and the Tianxiong land a loss in 937 and a gain in 938. (3) Thin item, Sixteen Prefectures (Taizong of Liao page opened): it dates the agreement to the 936 enthronement and gives no year for the handover, so 'promised 936, ceded 938' (Sixteen Prefectures page, three times 938, once 937) stands; ea-05's liao-dynasty must still reconcile with Cliopatria's Liao shape, which holds the land from 936.
